home.title: The TerraTools home screen
notes: Sidebar: every tool, grouped as Trait Mapping, Genomic Selection and Data Analysis. Click a name to open it.
Quick open (Ctrl+K): type part of a tool's name and press Enter.

interface_tour.title: Anatomy of a tool page
notes: Back: returns to the screen you came from (Alt+← also works).
Breadcrumbs: where you are. Click Home to return to the dashboard.
Tabs: most tools have an input tab first and a Results tab that opens automatically when a run finishes.
File box: click Browse to choose a file. The path appears here once it is loaded.
Run bar: starts the analysis. The line underneath shows progress and any error.
Collapse the sidebar to gain screen width.

mendelian_input.title: Mendelian Segregation — input and settings
notes: Genotype CSV: Marker, Chromosome, then one column per individual (0 / 1 / 2).
Population type: every type has its own model (RIL and DH 1:1, BC1 1:1, F2 1:2:1, F3 3:2:3, F4 7:2:7); the note below the list shows the one chosen.
Threshold (alpha) and the multiple-testing correction applied to the p-values (FDR by default).
Values to treat as missing, separated by commas.

mendelian_results.title: Mendelian Segregation — results
notes: Segregation plot (Manhattan): −log10(p) of every marker along the file, one colour per chromosome. Points above the dashed cut-off of the chosen correction are distorted markers.
Heterozygosity plot: the percentage of heterozygous calls of every marker, coloured by chromosome.
Distortion summary: the percentage of distorted markers on each chromosome.
Downloads: markers that pass the test, the full table and the LM-ready file for Linkage Mapping.
Summary: markers tested, inconclusive, flagged distorted, passing the quality check, and calls outside the model.

linkage_upload.title: Linkage Mapping — Upload tab
notes: Genotype Excel file: Marker, Chromosome, then one column per individual coded 0 / 1 / 2 / −1.
Population type: F2 or RIL.
Genotypes from a genotyping company (HapMap, VCF, A:G calls)? Convert them with the Genofile Converter first.
Preview of the first rows — check that columns were read as expected.
Markers found per chromosome.

linkage_params.title: Linkage Mapping — Parameters tab
notes: Missing-data limit, maximum recombination fraction, optional segregation-distortion filter and map scaling.
What each parameter does.

linkage_results.title: Linkage Mapping — Results tab
notes: Ready-to-use input file for QTL Mapping: the map positions with the same markers, transposed.
Excel exports: full results, all markers with positions, retained markers and recombination table.

linkage_map.title: Linkage Mapping — Map Plot tab
notes: Choose chromosomes, theme, colours and sizes, then click Update Plot.
The linkage map: each bar is a linkage group, ticks are markers, positions in cM (Kosambi).

qtl_input.title: QTL Mapping — input files and settings
notes: Genotype CSV: three header rows (marker names, chromosome, position in cM), then one row per individual.
Phenotype CSV: first column = individual ID, one column per trait.
Trait: choose the phenotype column to map.
Mapping method: SIM, CIM and MQM are regression methods; RF, SVR and XGBoost are machine-learning scores.
Threshold: a fixed LOD, or a genome-wide permutation test.
Support-interval LOD drop: 1.5 gives roughly a 95% interval around each peak.

qtl_results.title: QTL Mapping — results
notes: Downloads: the Manhattan and ideogram figures, the QTL table and the full scan of every marker.
LOD curve of every chromosome; shaded bands are the QTL regions.
The chromosomes with every QTL as a bar between its flanking markers and a dot at the peak; the dot grows with the LOD.

qtl_table.title: QTL Mapping — the QTL table
notes: One row per QTL: left, peak and right flanking marker, interval size, LOD, p-value, effects.
Scroll the table sideways for more columns (effect size, PVE, confidence intervals).

gene_input.title: Genes Extraction — input files
notes: The QTL Intervals file or the QTL table of QTL Mapping (Chromosome, Start, End) — or click “Use QTL Mapping output” to take the last QTL Mapping run.
Marker, Chromosome and bp columns, which place the QTL (in cM) on the genome. With no map, choose “No map: use a VCF”.
Gene annotation; the genes inside each interval are read from its gene lines.
Adds the sequence of every gene.
For a QTL table: confidence interval or flanking markers; and whether a gene must lie completely inside the region.

gene_results.title: Genes Extraction — genes in the region
notes: Each QTL region (with the basis of its interval) and the number of genes in it.

gene_results_genes.title: Genes Extraction — genes in gene regions
notes: The genes with their annotation details; the buttons underneath download the gene ID list, the table and the sequences.

pybsa_input.title: PYBSA G-statistics — input and settings
notes: Parents file: GATK4 table (tab or comma separated) with CHROM, POS, REF, ALT and GT / AD / GQ columns for the two parents.
Bulks file: the same layout for the two bulks (columns named <bulk>.GT, <bulk>.AD, <bulk>.GQ).
Number of individuals in each bulk, population type (F2, RIL, BC), p-value cut-offs and simulation replications.
Sliding-window size and step (bp), smoothing, read length.
Optional region of interest, GQ cut-off and other filters.

pybsa_results.title: PYBSA G-statistics — results
notes: Sub-tabs: the HTML report, plots, every output file and the log.

qtlseq_reads.title: QTL-Seq — starting from sequencing reads
notes: Start from sequencing reads (FASTQ or sorted BAM) or from a VCF.
Reference genome (FASTA, needed for FASTQ) and the parent, bulk 1 and bulk 2 reads. R2 files are optional (paired-end).
Individuals in each bulk and the population type: used to simulate the confidence intervals.
Read-depth limits, minimum SNP-index, window / step size (bp) and simulation replicates.

qtlseq_vcf.title: QTL-Seq — starting from a VCF
notes: VCF (.vcf or .vcf.gz) with a parent column and the two bulk columns; each needs an AD (allele depth) field.
Sample names as written in the VCF header (leave blank to use the first three columns in order).
Bulk sizes and population type.

qtlseq_results.title: QTL-Seq — results
notes: SNPs analysed, windows and the number of QTL regions found.
QTL regions: stretches where Δ(SNP-index) leaves the confidence interval.
Top and middle panels: SNP-index of each bulk. Bottom: Δ(SNP-index) with the 95% (dashed) and 99% (dotted) limits; shaded = QTL.

diversity_input.title: Diversity Analysis — input and settings
notes: CSV: column 1 = Variety, column 2 = Sample ID, columns 3+ = haplotype block codes (−1 or blank = missing).
Groups for hierarchical clustering.
How many of the most informative blocks to show.
Plot the variety radar on a 0–1 scale or with real mean values.

diversity_results.title: Diversity Analysis — results summary
notes: Summary of the dataset and of every diversity metric (mean ± standard deviation, range), per variety and per cluster.

gwas_3k.title: GWAS — rice 3K panel (phenotype file only)
notes: Genotype source: the built-in rice 3K panel, your own VCF, or a ready-made GWAS file.
Phenotype file: first column = accession ID exactly as in the panel (IRIS_313-…), other columns = traits.
Trait: pick the column to analyse.
Downloads all 2,229 accession IDs with an empty trait column to fill in.

gwas_vcf.title: GWAS — your own genotypes as a VCF
notes: VCF (.vcf / .vcf.gz) with genotype calls (GT). Only biallelic SNPs on numbered chromosomes are used.
Phenotype file: first column = sample ID exactly as in the VCF header.
Trait to analyse.

gwas_results.title: GWAS — results tables
notes: Downloads: Excel report, MTA table, the GWAS-ready file built from your phenotype data, and all plots.
MTA table: every marker that passes the permutation LOD threshold, per model.
One row per model, with genomic inflation (lambda).

gwas_plots.title: GWAS — plots
notes: Manhattan plot: LOD per marker; diamonds are MTAs.
QQ plot: points on the diagonal mean a well-calibrated test.

clustering_input.title: Clustering & Genomic Selection — input
notes: CSV or TSV: sample IDs in the first column, one column per SNP (0 / 1 / 2, −1 = missing).
K for K-means clustering.
Fraction of each cluster held out as the testing set.
How many principal components K-means uses (0 = all of them). A few leading components keep the population structure and drop noise.

clustering_results.title: Clustering & Genomic Selection — results
notes: Samples, markers, clusters, train / test sizes and variance explained by PC1 and PC2.
PCA plot coloured by K-means cluster.
Under the K-selection plot (silhouette width and within-cluster sum of squares for K = 2 to 10; red = the K you used, gold = the highest silhouette), the note says which K the data support.
Downloads: training and testing genotype files (cluster-stratified), cluster membership and the plot.

additive_input.title: Additive Dominance — input
notes: CSV or TSV: sample IDs in the first column, SNP markers after (0 / 1 / 2). Blank cells are missing.
How missing genotypes are filled.
Additive, dominance or both relationship matrices.

additive_results.title: Additive Dominance — results
notes: Samples, SNPs, missing data and markers with MAF > 0.05.
Heatmap of the additive relationship matrix (clusters of related lines show as blocks).
Sub-tabs: Heatmaps, Histogram, Data Table and Downloads (CSV of each matrix).

breedsight_input.title: BreedSight Genomic Prediction — input and settings
notes: Training phenotypes: sample_id, phenotypes.
Training genotypes: sample_id, then SNP columns (0 / 1 / 2), no missing values.
Testing phenotypes: sample_id and an optional phenotypes column.
Testing genotypes: same SNP columns as the training file.
Number of folds and the trait heritability used in the interpretation.

breedsight_results.title: BreedSight Genomic Prediction — results
notes: Accuracy of every model (BreedSight DNN+RF, Lasso, RBLUP, GBLUP) on training and validation data.
Sub-tabs: metrics and interpretation, test predictions, plots, downloads.

heterosis_input.title: Heterosis — input files and parameters
notes: Training phenotype CSV: column 0 = sample ID, column 1 = numeric trait value.
Training genotype CSV: first column = sample ID, then numeric marker columns. Row order must match the phenotype file.
Parent genotype CSV: first column = parent ID, same marker columns as the training file.
Test genotype CSV (optional): same marker columns, for out-of-sample predictions.
Number of hybrids / parents to report, cross-validation folds and network settings.

heterosis_results.title: Heterosis — results
notes: Top F1 hybrids, top parents, all hybrid results and test predictions as CSV.
Prediction accuracy from cross-validation (MSE, RMSE, R², Pearson r).
Best hybrid combinations with GEBV, mid-parent (MPH) and better-parent (BPH) heterosis.

phenotypic_input.title: Phenotypic Data Analysis — data and design
notes: CSV or Excel, one row per plot. Genotype, Environment, Rep (and Block) columns are found by name; every other numeric column is a trait. The file is read once and shared by every analysis.
Augmented RCBD, RCBD or alpha-lattice: decides the blocking terms of the models.
Analyse all environments or only chosen ones; 0 can count as missing.
Layout of every environment: plots, accessions, replications, blocks and checks.

phenotypic_results.title: Phenotypic Data Analysis — an analysis tab
notes: One tab per analysis: descriptives, environments, BLUEs, ANOVA, heritability, correlation, PCA, clustering and stability.
Each analysis has its own traits and options, and its own Run button.

phenotypic_heritability.title: Phenotypic Data Analysis — heritability
notes: Variance components and heritability (entry-mean and plot basis) per trait and environment.

diversity_plots.title: Diversity Analysis — charts
notes: Sub-tabs: block analysis, metrics heatmap, variety comparison, PCA & clustering, NJ tree and the results table.
Every chart is a PNG on a white background; click it to open it in a pop-up, or use Download PNG. Here: PCA coloured by variety, and by cluster.

geneprio_input.title: Gene Prioritization — species, trait and inputs
notes: Species (rice, wheat or maize) and the trait in words; related terms are added automatically.
The genes to rank: paste IDs or choose a TXT / CSV / Excel file, for example the Gene_ID_list.txt of Genes Extraction.
An option to ignore the cached answers and ask the databases again.
Ensembl Plants, Gramene, Plant Reactome, NCBI and (rice) Oryzabase: press Check connections to test them.

geneprio_summary.title: Gene Prioritization — summary
notes: How many genes were read, annotated and linked to the trait.
The top genes with their final score from the databases.
Downloads: ranked list (CSV), workbook with all evidence (Excel) and report (HTML).

geneprio_ranking.title: Gene Prioritization — ranked genes
notes: Search by gene, symbol or description.
Click a column to sort, a row to open the evidence. A dash means no evidence of that kind could be retrieved; it is not a score of zero.

geneprio_evidence.title: Gene Prioritization — evidence behind one gene
notes: The gene, its rank, position and source links.
Score of every evidence category and how many points it added to the final score.

cross_markers_input.title: Optimal Cross Selection — input files
notes: Allele dosage matrix: genotypes in the rows, markers in the columns, values 0 / 1 / 2. The relationship matrix is calculated from it.
Marker effects: the columns Marker and Effect.
Genetic map: Marker, Chromosome and cM, to predict the variance of the progeny.
Number of crosses, penalty degree, and the population type, generation, selected proportion and candidate pool.

cross_markers_results.title: Optimal Cross Selection — usefulness of the crosses
notes: Crosses, parents, the expected usefulness of the plan, group coancestry and progeny inbreeding.
Each cross with its usefulness, mean and progeny standard deviation.

cross_markers_vcf.title: Optimal Cross Selection — a VCF instead of a genetic map
notes: Choose this when you have no genetic map.
The VCF: its CHROM, POS and ID columns give the position of every marker.
The rate that turns base pairs into cM, the same for the whole genome.

diversity_tree.title: Diversity Analysis — circular neighbour-joining tree
notes: Circular tree: pale sectors mark the varieties, concentric circles give the genetic distance, red triangles are branches supported by at least 70% of bootstrap trees. Click to enlarge.

diversity_popup.title: Diversity Analysis — the tree opened in a pop-up

phenotypic_anova.title: Phenotypic Data Analysis — ANOVA
notes: One table per trait: every environment and the pooled analysis side by side (DF, SS, MS, F, P, significance), with plots, mean and CV underneath.

genotype_input.title: Genotype Viewer — file, species, drawing mode, colours and image quality
notes: Genotype file: CSV or VCF. The first column is the chromosome, then the marker name, the position (bp) and one column per sample; the column names do not matter.
Species whose chromosome lengths are used. The chromosome names of the file are matched to its names (1, chr1 and chr01 are the same).
Name some samples to draw only those; empty draws every sample.
Normal: one image per sample. Compare: one image per chromosome with all samples side by side. Zoomed: one region of one chromosome for all samples.
2 or 3 colours, fill between markers, marker names (and, in compare / zoomed mode, the dashed line from each name).
GenoSee's palettes (bright, Aqua, grays, reds, blues) and a mixed red-blue-yellow-grey palette.
Words that replace REF / ALT / HET in the legend, for example the names of the two parents.
PNG resolution (200, 300 or 600 dpi) and an extra vector PDF for publication.

genotype_results.title: Genotype Viewer — the graphical genotypes
notes: Images drawn, samples, markers and chromosomes.
One image per sample (normal mode): each chromosome is a bar coloured by the genotype; the legend is at the right.

favallele_setup.title: Favourable Allele Analysis — matched marker IDs, filters and lines
notes: Markers in your file, how many of the trait-gene markers were found by ID, the trait genes covered and the number of lines.
Every ID of your file that matched, with the gene, the trait and how it was matched. Download matched IDs saves the list as CSV.
Restrict the traits and genes (the list follows the traits) and choose the status to show.
Search and tick the lines of your file. The coloured names are the selected ones: click a name to make it the line shown in detail, × removes it.

favallele_overview.title: Favourable Allele Analysis — overview of the selected line
notes: The selected lines (click one to show it in detail) and the filters in force. Change takes you back to the file tab.
SNP and gene counts of the line shown: favourable, unfavourable, heterozygous and missing.
One dot for every gene, placed on the plant part that the trait belongs to. Hover for the gene, click for all its SNPs; colour the dots by trait or by allele status.
Number of SNPs of the chosen status for every trait, one bar per selected line.

favallele_gene.title: Favourable Allele Analysis — the details of one gene
notes: Trait, position and the status of every SNP of the gene in every selected line (REF/ALT written out as the two nucleotides).

favallele_genes.title: Favourable Allele Analysis — genes and the allele map
notes: A bar per gene for the line shown: favourable, heterozygous, unfavourable and missing SNPs.
Rows are the selected lines, columns the SNPs of each gene, coloured by status — to see where the lines differ.

favallele_heatmap_setup.title: Favourable Allele Analysis — Heatmap tab: genes and lines
notes: Pick genes from the list (search by name), add all the genes of a trait with one click, or take the genes of the filters.
Pick lines from the list, or take all the lines of your file.
Resolution of the PNG.

favallele_heatmap.title: Favourable Allele Analysis — the balloon heatmap
notes: Genes and lines drawn, markers used after the quality control, and the size of the figure.

Balloon heatmap drawn by the R script: balloon size and blue depth show the fraction of a gene's markers at which the line is homozygous favourable; a cross is no call. Coloured strip: trait of the gene; bars: favourable alleles per line.

favallele_upload_empty.title: Favourable Allele Analysis — scope and the genotype file
notes: Scope: the tool is for the rice 4K haplopanel only, for now. The trait-gene markers are kept inside TerraTools; it is not scaled to other panels or crops yet.
Your 4K haplopanel genotypes: one row per marker, one column per line; 0 / 1 / 2 / -1, VCF genotypes or nucleotides.

genofile_input.title: Genofile Converter — a VCF, its parents and the output settings
notes: The company file: HapMap, VCF / VCF.GZ or an Excel / CSV sheet of allele calls. The format is detected; change it with the buttons if it is wrong.
How an individual is coded against the two parents, and when a marker is left out.
Choose Parent 1 and Parent 2 among the samples of the file (P1 and P2 were found automatically); samples that do not belong to the population can be left out.
Marker names (as in the file or chromosome_position), chromosome labels (Chr01 becomes 1) and whether markers on scaffolds are left out.

genofile_result.title: Genofile Converter — the converted files
notes: Markers in the file, coded (kept), left out, individuals and the share of calls that are missing or unexpected.
What the file contains (a row per marker, a column per individual, coded 0 / 1 / 2 / −1), the CSV and Excel downloads, and shortcuts to continue in another tool.
Parent missing, parent heterozygous, or both parents with the same allele; the genotype codes of all kept markers are counted on the right.

recomb_input.title: Recombination Analysis — file, parent and smoothing
notes: The genotype table: a row per marker (CHROM, POS, ID …) and a column per sample, coded 0 / 1 / 2 / −1. The page reports markers, chromosomes, samples and the share of heterozygous and missing calls.
The recurrent parent (found automatically), an optional genotyped donor, and samples to leave out.
Smoothing method and minimum block: the setting that changes the crossover counts most. Also the bin size of the rate plot and the centromere shading.

recomb_result.title: Recombination Analysis — results
notes: Lines, informative markers, crossovers, mean per line, mean donor % and the share of intragenic crossovers.
Warnings about the data: lines with mostly missing calls, very heterozygous lines, and how precisely a crossover is located.
Crossovers per line and chromosome, the genome-wide crossover rate, donor content, the haplotype mosaic, a circos plot and the intragenic / intergenic split.
One Excel workbook with every table, a ZIP with CSV files and figures, and the main tables as CSV.

insilico_input.title: In silico BSA — genotype file, phenotype file, pools and windows
notes: The genotype table: CHROM, POS, then one column per line, coded 0 / 1 / 2 / −1. The page reports the markers, chromosomes, lines and the share of heterozygous and missing calls.
The phenotype file: line names in the first column, then the traits. Not needed when the genotype file already has a trait column.
The share of lines in each pool (20 % = the lowest and the highest fifth) and the population type, which you choose yourself.
The primary window, the minimum markers per window, the distance for merging regions, the permutations and the significance level.

insilico_result.title: In silico BSA — loci, regions and figures
notes: Lines, lines per pool, markers, loci, regions of all window sizes and the Gw threshold of the primary window.
Regions of the three window sizes that overlap are one locus; the table says how many sizes found it and how far apart their peaks lie.

Where the ΔSNP-index (high pool − low pool) lies outside the 99 % interval of random pools: the SNP-index of each pool at the peak, the sign of the difference and which pool carries the allele of the chosen parent.
One row per region and window size: left, peak and right marker with their positions, adjusted p-value, LOD and the allele-frequency difference.
Lists the genes of a GFF3 / GTF annotation that lie in a region, widened by a flank.

The SNP-index of the high pool, of the low pool and the ΔSNP-index along the genome (first figure), then Gw for the three window sizes, the loci, Gw against the allele-frequency statistics, the genotype classes in the two pools, the trait distribution and the permutation null.

qtl_compare.title: QTL Mapping — Compare Models
notes: Tick the methods to compare and click Run Comparison; the settings of the Analysis tab are used.
One lane and one colour per method on the chromosome map: SIM pink, CIM red, MQM orange, RF grey, SVR light blue, XGBoost purple.
How many regions each method found.
One row per region: flanking and peak markers, size, how many methods found it, which ones, and the mean and maximum LOD and PVE.

mendelian_results_skewed.title: Mendelian Segregation — a population that is not a RIL
notes: Almost every marker is far above the cut-off on every chromosome: a genome-wide skew, not a few distorted regions.
The share of distorted markers is high (63 to 95 %) on all twelve chromosomes.
Summary: 3,687 of 4,454 tested markers are distorted against 1 : 1.

mendelian_results_4k.title: Mendelian Segregation — a dense RIL map
notes: Most markers sit near zero; three regions rise above the dashed cut-off (chromosomes 3, 6 and 9): real distortion regions.
Heterozygosity: low (about 1 %) along all chromosomes, as in an advanced RIL.
Distortion summary: concentrated on chromosomes 3, 6 and 9.

insilico_snpindex.title: In silico BSA — SNP-index of the high pool (A) and the low pool (B), ΔSNP-index with its intervals (C) and the strongest region (D)
